entry.hops: No wire in the Node test: the daemon client is the real session service called in process; replies are recorded as the objects returned (and their JSON byte size, a measure). A replay over the real daemon wire records the same reply objects.
entry.notRun: no real store or runtime; the viewer is one local client token
entry.runs: createSessionService (subscribeSession, readSession) with a scripted readStoredSession over 300 rows, SessionHostTransport.readSession, SessionHostPublication (projections, applySessionResult, applyTranscriptPage, heldTranscript), SessionTranscriptWindows

normalised.reason: per-run temp path (or generated name) replaced by a placeholder

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: the core's answers to the recorded reads whole (rows, hasOlder), and the rows the desktop client displays at the end of each case against the recorded snapshot.items whole
replay.entry: Two replays. (1) What the core itself answers: thread/items/list (mixdog-core-session/src/session/reads.rs items_list) over a real store, session_host_replay_tests (an_older_page_answers_only_the_revealed_rows_as_node_recorded, a_session_that_changed_between_reads_answers_the_recorded_window_as_node_recorded, held_rows_that_move_during_a_page_read_fall_back_to_a_full_read_as_node_recorded), each compared whole with the recording. (2) What the user then sees: the desktop client code (protocol client, host adapter createChatApi + createChatHostApi, renderer hook useTranscriptWindow with its pager) run against the built mixdogd over its WebSocket listener: node --import ./apps/desktop/scripts/test-env.mjs --import ./apps/desktop/scripts/test-tsx.mjs benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/replay-session-host-transcript-page.mjs --mixdogd <exe> --seeds <dir with c300 and c302, each laid by `cargo-gate.ps1 run -p mixdog-app-server-daemon --example seed_transcript_page_session -- <dir>/c300` and `... -- <dir>/c302 n0 n1`>

normalised.rowIds: a row id is the core's item id where the recorder scripted c0..c299; the rows are compared whole without it
normalised.rowText: the recorder handed its scripted rows to the host untrimmed (`row <id> ` x50); a stored assistant message restores as its trimmed text in Node (transcript-restore/restore.mjs restoredAssistantTranscriptItems) and in the core alike, so the recorded text is compared trimmed
normalised.pageShape: Node's host reply wrapper (page/full, projectionStamp, byte size) is the desktop host's; the core answers the same rows and hasOlder on thread/items/list (older page by the opening page's nextCursor; full read without a cursor)
normalised.seeding: a connection cannot store rows: the core runs over a data directory whose session (the 300 recorded rows c0..c299, and n0, n1 for the changed session) the core's own row writer laid (the seed_transcript_page_session example, thread/inheritedRows/append)
normalised.olderPage: an older page crosses ...: in the K1 chain the reader following the tail grows its window by a page (the hook's window growth: the 32 rows held + 64, read from the core by prefetchSession); the displayed rows are compared whole with the recorded snapshot.items. Nothing else is excluded
normalised.changedBetweenReads: a session that changed between reads: the client holds the core's feed, so the appended rows are among its held rows once the feed frames are applied; Node's state (32 rows held, 2 more in the core) exists here while those frames are not yet applied, i.e. while the page is in flight. The replay holds the pager's page read in flight, then the client's held rows are the 34 (the tail moved); the pager drops the page and the hook reads the window the request was made for (32 held + 64 = 96 rows), and the 96 rows displayed are compared whole with the recorded snapshot.items
normalised.inFlightMovement: held rows that move while the page is in flight: the held rows are the desktop host's own copy in Node (session-host-publication.ts heldTranscript), the recorder changed only that copy; here the hook is given the held rows without their first, while the pager's page read is held in flight. The pager drops the page and the hook reads the window the request was made for (32 + 64 = 96 rows, not 31 + 64), and the 96 rows displayed are compared whole with the recorded snapshot.items
